title: Professional native-first synthesis and DSP
scope: Synthesizer sound generation, DSP fidelity, quality qualification and cross-host rendering; complements docs/song-rollout.md instead of replacing its Song-specific stages.
mission: Deliver professionally viable editable instruments that sound correct in native desktop/mobile production and natively in pre-programmed, while retaining a compatible web studio wherever technically feasible.

platform_policy.web: maintain_when_feasible; never constrain native audio quality to Web Audio or web packaging limits
platform_policy.professional_quality_gate: native reference implementations must pass acoustic and CPU benchmarks even if web support requires an explicit degraded mode
platform_policy.portability: portable patch/automation/event semantics with host-specific DSP implementations verified by reference fixtures
platform_policy.real_time: avoid allocation, blocking I/O, locks and GC-sensitive work in audio callback
platform_policy.backwards_compatibility: version schema when interpretation changes; maintain documented migrations and legacy reads
platform_policy.data_storage: store audio bytes as external assets; keep .premidi files declarative and inspectable

architectural_decisions.decision: Separate platform-neutral synth graph and parameter/event semantics from the current Web Audio voice implementation.
architectural_decisions.implemented_scope: versioned amplitude-envelope event plan and Web Audio adapter; remaining graph contracts unimplemented

architectural_decisions.decision: Prototype suitable portable DSP engines/frameworks for native desktop/mobile before committing to C++, Rust, JUCE, WebAssembly or another specific toolchain.
Use shared test fixtures and reference audio analysis to establish host parity; bit-identical floating-point samples are not assumed across implementations.
architectural_decisions.implemented_scope: host-neutral PCM metrics and tolerant acoustic fingerprints; current measured backend is Chromium offline Web Audio only

architectural_decisions.decision: Introduce a new versioned synth patch schema only when its meaning changes; do not break existing v7 Beat/v8 Song imports.
Web compatibility is best effort without silent sound substitutions; capabilities and unsupported features must be detectable.

must_pass: browser regression checks on compatible PRs
verification_policy.thresholds: document test inputs, reference hardware and tolerances before claiming an objective performance metric
non_goals: claim state-of-the-art quality on feature count alone
silently replace native sounds with samples
sacrifice native DSP to preserve browser support

usability_gate.principle: Professional complexity underneath, immediate musical control on the surface
usability_gate.applies_to: All synthesis, host, automation and sound-editing roadmap tasks
acceptance: A preset can be previewed, selected and heard from the current inspector
Volume, brightness, attack and release remain directly reachable without a beginner/expert mode switch
The same authored parameters back common controls and deeper editing; no duplicate competing systems
A saved variation preserves the edited sound and volume and can be reopened on desktop and mobile
Each new capability earns its UI space and has sound-specific accessible label help
usability_gate.human_qualification: Observed newcomer comprehension and musical listening signoff remain explicit release requirements; successful clicks are not evidence of intuitive understanding

phases.title: Native applications, game integration and qualification

tasks.title: Correct note-off and envelope state
acceptance: An early release begins from the actual attack/decay level, with no jump to sustain.
Long notes retain intended ADSR durations.
Synth preview and offline rendering use the same envelope contract.

verification.method: 18 constant-input rendered ADSR cases against an independent analytical oracle; overlapping and retriggered production voices at three sample rates
verification.shared_runtime: live transport, audition, conversion preview and WAV export all use scheduleNote -> scheduleAmplitudeEnvelope -> planAmplitudeEnvelope
verification.compatibility: preserves 2 ms attack floor, zero-decay sustain step and 0.000001 release floor; unchanged stored patch v1 and Beat v7/Song v8
verification.scope: current ADSR scheduling contract; physical live-device loopback and native DSP equivalence are later host qualification

tasks.title: Oversampled nonlinear drive
acceptance: Distortion on synth and sampler uses 4x oversampled WaveShaper where supported.
Spectrum benchmarks quantify aliasing at representative pitches and drive settings.
Native DSP backend reproduces equivalent anti-aliasing behavior.

verification.method: bin-coherent high sine into identical drive curve at 0.25 and 0.8, none versus 4x, at 44.1/48/96 kHz
verification.performance: offline setup-plus-render medians recorded after warm-up, not a real-time CPU guarantee
remaining: native oversampling parity depends on SYN-007
absolute alias floor across more signals and filter implementations
real-time device CPU and latency qualification

tasks.title: Measured audio quality regression harness
acceptance: Automated tests measure alias-to-signal energy, DC offset, peaks, attack/release discontinuities and RMS.
Reference renders and threshold metadata are versioned; regressions fail CI.
Test results distinguish browser/device variance from DSP defects.
tasks.dependency_rationale: Measurements are prerequisites for verifying SYN-001/002, not successors; no native backend is required to establish current browser baselines.

verification.environment: CHROME_BIN selects a Chromium executable; no runtime/npm dependencies
coverage: seeded noise and harmonic repeated renders
4x drive alias reduction and offline wall time
limitations: off-harmonic residual is a fixture-specific alias proxy with masked-harmonic blind spots
timings are offline wall times on a virtualized host, not real-time CPU qualification
native backend and hardware loopback parity remain unverified

tasks.title: Polyphony and shared voice lifecycle
acceptance: Voice budget and stealing policy are explicit and deterministic.
32 sustained voices are glitch-free on a specified desktop reference configuration.
Stop/seek/loop cannot leak oscillators or drop shared delay tails.

implemented: release-first/oldest deterministic stealing with vocal priority
5 ms source fade and cancellation of future starts
owned synth, modulation, noise, sample and vocal source cleanup
identical linear delay buses shared per session; tails survive steals
feedback-derived live completion and Beat/Song WAV tail lengths
verification.realtime_scope: AudioWorklet capture of 32 sustained expressive voices in the browser rendering graph, with finite/peak/RMS/silent-block and cleanup gates
remaining: real output-device underrun/latency qualification on documented desktop/mobile hardware
native allocation-free callback implementation and CPU scaling tests under SYN-007
MIDI sustain pedal handling under SYN-016
limitations: The logical budget excludes retiring-source overlap during the 5 ms fade
Shared delay tails do not consume pitched-voice budget
Browser callback graph capture cannot observe driver-side underruns

tasks.title: Master headroom, monitoring and export fidelity
acceptance: Peak/RMS and true-peak measurement report clipping rather than concealing it.
16-/24-bit PCM and 32-bit float output paths are specified, with dithering where appropriate.
Export sample-rate conversion meets a measured fidelity target.

tasks.title: Host-neutral synth graph and versioned DSP contracts
acceptance: Patch and note interpretation produces a versioned JSON synth plan without DOM, microphone, IndexedDB or AudioNode objects.
Existing oscillator, harmonic, filter, ADSR, expression, effects and routing parameter identifiers, units, defaults and interpolation policy are explicit without changing patch v1 persistence.

The current Web Audio adapter renders serialized canonical plans within measured tolerances of the pre-refactor implementation; native/game adapters consume this contract and are separately qualified in SYN-007/SYN-020.
tasks.dependency_rationale: Canonical envelope semantics and fixtures can proceed before native oversampling parity; requiring completed SYN-002 would implicitly block the native backend needed to finish it.

verification.reference_method: Render actual previous-commit code in an isolated local namespace, compare six musical fixture sounds at three sample rates; separately measure original and current repeatability. A serialized voice plan is rendered through the current adapter.

acceptance_adjustment.reason: Separate completion of the portable representation and working compatibility adapter from creation of future native/game hosts; otherwise SYN-007 depends on a task that cannot finish before SYN-007 exists. Native parity is retained as a mandatory later gate, not claimed here.

tasks.title: Real-time native DSP host design
acceptance: Choose and document a maintained native DSP toolchain and mobile/desktop audio-device adapters based on prototypes.
Audio callback performs no unbounded allocation, I/O, locks or UI work.
Device sample-rate, buffer-size, underrun and suspend/resume behavior is tested.

tasks.title: Web host compatibility adapter
acceptance: Web support may fall back only through declared and user-visible compatibility modes.
Web limitations cannot reduce native synthesis capability or corrupt native patches.
Unsupported capabilities do not silently render as a different instrument.

tasks.title: General modulation matrix
acceptance: Velocity, key tracking, envelopes and LFOs can target multiple supported synthesis parameters.
Bipolar/unipolar ranges, depth, polarity and modulation rate are explicit.
Modulation is deterministic under offline rendering and gameplay control.

Keep advanced controls contextual in the same Sound inspector and preserve saved variations

tasks.title: Newcomer sound-design and musical-reference qualification
acceptance: Desktop and phone workflows cover preview, selection, hearing, brightness/volume/onset/fade edits, native export, save and reload of a variation.
A small set of musical sounds has versioned acoustic compatibility fixtures and audible control-response checks.
Observed newcomer sessions and listening review confirm comprehension and musical usefulness without requiring oscillator or modulation mathematics.

interface_changes: Cutoff, Attack and Release share a compact first group with no duplicate controls

human_review.no_claim: Automated action completion does not prove newcomer comprehension or musical polish
